text: When the boat bumped against the posts, the boatmen called out Arsats name, but no answer came from the house, and the silence seemed to grow deeper. <break time="0.8s" /> The chief boatman announced sulkily that they would cook and sleep in the boat on the open water, and the white man, asking only for his blankets, climbed up alone. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Arsat came out of the low doorway, a young, broad chested man wearing only a sarong, and without any of the usual greetings he asked, Have you medicine, Tuan. <break time="0.8s" /> No, said the white man, startled, but why do you ask, Is there sickness in the house, and Arsat answered only, Enter and see, turning back into the dim house. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside, on a raised couch of bamboo, lay a woman covered with a red cloth, her eyes wide open but seeing nothing, as if she were staring at something far away. <break time="0.8s" /> Her cheeks burned with a high fever, and the white man, seeing the stillness of her face, understood at once that she was very close to death. <break time="0.8s" /> She hears nothing now, Tuan, Arsat said, and I have not slept for five nights, for at first she struggled, hearing voices calling her from the water. <break time="0.8s" /> Arsat asked in a low voice, Tuan, will she die, and the white man, looking at the still face on the couch, could only answer sadly that he feared so.
